verses.zh: 律法既是将来美事的影儿，不是本物的真像，总不能藉着每年常献一样的祭物叫那近前来的人得以完全。
verses.en: For the law possesses a shadow of the good things to come but not the reality itself, and is therefore completely unable, by the same sacrifices offered continually, year after year, to perfect those who come to worship.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “those who approach.”

verses.zh: 若不然，献祭的事岂不早已止住了吗？因为礼拜的人，良心既被洁净，就不再觉得有罪了。
verses.en: For otherwise would they not have ceased to be offered, since the worshipers would have been purified once for all and so have[NOTE:1] no further consciousness of sin?
notes: Grk “the worshipers, having been purified once for all, would have.”

verses.zh: 但这些祭物是叫人每年想起罪来；
verses.en: But in those sacrifices[NOTE:1] there is a reminder of sins year after year.
notes: Grk “in them”; the referent (those sacrifices) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 因为公牛和山羊的血，断不能除罪。
verses.en: For it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

verses.zh: 所以基督到世上来的时候，就说：　神啊，祭物和礼物是你不愿意的；你曾给我预备了身体。
verses.en: So when he came into the world, he said,“Sacrifice and offering you did not desire, but a body you prepared for me.

verses.zh: 燔祭和赎罪祭是你不喜欢的。
verses.en: Whole burnt offerings and sin-offerings you took no delight in.

verses.zh: 那时我说：　神啊，我来了，为要照你的旨意行；我的事在经卷上已经记载了。
verses.en: Then I said, ‘Here I am:[NOTE:1] I have come—it is written of me in the scroll of the book—to do your will, O God.’”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “behold,” but this construction often means “here is/there is” (cf. BDAG 468 s.v. ἰδού 2).
A quotation from Ps 40:6-8 (LXX). The phrase a body you prepared for me (in v. 5) is apparently an interpretive expansion of the HT reading “ears you have dug out for me.”

verses.zh: 以上说：「祭物和礼物，燔祭和赎罪祭，是你不愿意的，也是你不喜欢的（这都是按着律法献的）」；
verses.en: When he says above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and sin-offerings you did not desire nor did you take delight in them”[NOTE:1] (which are offered according to the law),
notes: Various phrases from the quotation of Ps 40:6 in Heb 10:5-6 are repeated in Heb 10:8.

verses.zh: 后又说：「我来了为要照你的旨意行」；可见他是除去在先的，为要立定在后的。
verses.en: then he says, “Here I am: I have come to do your will.”[NOTE:1] He does away with[NOTE:2] the first to establish the second.
notes: The majority of mss, especially the later ones (א2 0278vid 1739 M lat), have ὁ θεός (ho theos, “God”) at this point, while most of the earliest and best witnesses lack such an explicit addressee (so P46 א* A C D K P Ψ 33 1175 1881 2464 al). The longer reading is apparently motivated in part by the wording of Ps 40:8 (39:9 LXX) and by the word order of this same verse as quoted in Heb 10:7.
Or “abolishes.”

verses.zh: 我们凭这旨意，靠耶稣基督，只一次献上他的身体，就得以成圣。
verses.en: By his will[NOTE:1] we have been made holy through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
notes: Grk “by which will.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.

verses.zh: 凡祭司天天站着事奉　神，屡次献上一样的祭物，这祭物永不能除罪。
verses.en: And every priest stands day after day[NOTE:1] serving and offering the same sacrifices again and again—sacrifices that can never take away sins.
notes: Or “daily,” “every day.”

verses.zh: 但基督献了一次永远的赎罪祭，就在　神的右边坐下了。
verses.en: But when this priest[NOTE:1] had offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, he sat down at the right hand[NOTE:2] of God,
notes: Grk “this one.” This pronoun refers to Jesus, but “this priest” was used in the translation to make the contrast between the Jewish priests in v. 11 and Jesus as a priest clearer in English.
An allusion to Ps 110:1.

verses.zh: 从此，等候他仇敌成了他的脚凳。
verses.en: where he is now waiting[NOTE:1] until his enemies are made a footstool for his feet.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “from then on waiting.”
An allusion to Ps 110:1.

verses.zh: 因为他一次献祭，便叫那得以成圣的人永远完全。
verses.en: For by one offering he has perfected for all time those who are made holy.

verses.zh: 圣灵也对我们作见证；因为他既已说过：
verses.en: And the Holy Spirit also witnesses to us, for after saying,[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “after having said,” emphasizing the present impact of this utterance.

verses.zh: 主说：那些日子以后，我与他们所立的约乃是这样：我要将我的律法写在他们心上，又要放在他们的里面。
verses.en: “This is the covenant that I will establish with them after those days, says the Lord. I will put[NOTE:1] my laws on their hearts and I will inscribe them on their minds,”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “putting…I will inscribe.”
A quotation from Jer 31:33.

verses.zh: 以后就说：我不再记念他们的罪愆和他们的过犯。
verses.en: then he says,[NOTE:1] “Their sins and their lawless deeds I will remember no longer.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “and.”
A quotation from Jer 31:34.

verses.zh: 这些罪过既已赦免，就不用再为罪献祭了。
verses.en: Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer any offering for sin.

verses.zh: 弟兄们，我们既因耶稣的血得以坦然进入至圣所，
verses.en: Therefore, brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] since we have confidence to enter the sanctuary by the blood of Jesus,
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 2:11.

verses.zh: 是藉着他给我们开了一条又新又活的路，从幔子经过，这幔子就是他的身体。
verses.en: by the fresh and living way that he inaugurated for us[NOTE:1] through the curtain, that is, through his flesh,[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “that he inaugurated for us as a fresh and living way,” referring to the entrance mentioned in v. 19.

Through his flesh. In a bold shift the writer changes from a spatial phrase (Christ opened the way through the curtain into the inner sanctuary) to an instrumental phrase (he did this through [by means of] his flesh in his sacrifice of himself), associating the two in an allusion to the splitting of the curtain in the temple from top to bottom (Matt 27:51; Mark 15:38; Luke 23:45). Just as the curtain was split, so Christ’s body was broken for us, to give us access into God’s presence.

verses.zh: 又有一位大祭司治理　神的家，
verses.en: and since we have a great priest[NOTE:1] over the house of God,
notes: Grk “and a great priest,” continuing the construction begun in v. 19.

verses.zh: 并我们心中天良的亏欠已经洒去，身体用清水洗净了，就当存着诚心和充足的信心来到　神面前；
verses.en: let us draw near with a sincere heart in the assurance that faith brings,[NOTE:1] because we have had our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience[NOTE:2] and our bodies washed in pure water.
notes: Grk “in assurance of faith.”

The phrase our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience combines the OT imagery of the sprinkling with blood to give ritual purity with the emphasis on the interior cleansing provided by the new covenant: It is the heart that is cleansed and the conscience made perfect (cf. Heb 8:10; 9:9, 14; 10:2, 16).

verses.zh: 也要坚守我们所承认的指望，不至摇动，因为那应许我们的是信实的。
verses.en: And let us hold unwaveringly to the hope that we confess, for the one who made the promise is trustworthy.

verses.zh: 又要彼此相顾，激发爱心，勉励行善。
verses.en: And let us take thought of how to spur one another on to love and good works,[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “let us consider one another for provoking of love and good deeds.”

verses.zh: 你们不可停止聚会，好像那些停止惯了的人，倒要彼此劝勉，既知道（原文是看见）那日子临近，就更当如此。
verses.en: not abandoning our own meetings, as some are in the habit of doing, but encouraging each other, and even more so because you see the day[NOTE:1] drawing near.[NOTE:2]
notes: The day refers to that well-known time of Christ’s coming and judgment in the future; see a similar use of “day” in 1 Cor 3:13.

This paragraph (vv. 19-25) is actually a single, skillfully composed sentence in Greek, but it must be broken into shorter segments for English idiom. It begins with several subordinate phrases (since we have confidence and a great priest), has three parallel exhortations as its main verbs (let us draw near, hold, and take thought), and concludes with several subordinate phrases related to the final exhortation (not abandoning but encouraging).

verses.zh: 因为我们得知真道以后，若故意犯罪，赎罪的祭就再没有了；
verses.en: For if we deliberately keep on sinning after receiving the knowledge of the truth, no further sacrifice for sins is left for us,[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “is left,” with “for us” implied by the first half of the verse.

verses.zh: 惟有战惧等候审判和那烧灭众敌人的烈火。
verses.en: but only a certain fearful expectation of judgment and a fury[NOTE:1] of fire that will consume God’s enemies.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “zeal,” recalling God’s jealous protection of his holiness and honor (cf. Exod 20:5).sn An allusion to Zeph 1:18.
Grk “the enemies.”sn An allusion to Isa 26:11.

verses.zh: 人干犯摩西的律法，凭两三个见证人，尚且不得怜恤而死，
verses.en: Someone who rejected the law of Moses was put to death[NOTE:1] without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “dies.”
An allusion to Deut 17:6.

verses.zh: 何况人践踏　神的儿子，将那使他成圣之约的血当作平常，又亵慢施恩的圣灵，你们想，他要受的刑罚该怎样加重呢！
verses.en: How much greater punishment do you think that person deserves who has contempt for[NOTE:1] the Son of God, and profanes[NOTE:2] the blood of the covenant that made him holy,[NOTE:3] and insults the Spirit of grace?
notes: Grk “tramples under foot.”
Grk “regarded as common.”
Grk “by which he was made holy.”

verses.zh: 因为我们知道谁说：「伸冤在我，我必报应」；又说：「主要审判他的百姓。」
verses.en: For we know the one who said, “Vengeance is mine, I will repay,”[NOTE:1] and again, “The Lord will judge his people.”[NOTE:2]
notes: A quotation from Deut 32:35.
A quotation from Deut 32:36.

verses.zh: 落在永生　神的手里，真是可怕的！
verses.en: It is a terrifying thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

verses.zh: 你们要追念往日，蒙了光照以后所忍受大争战的各样苦难：
verses.en: But remember the former days when you endured a harsh conflict of suffering after you were enlightened.

verses.zh: 一面被毁谤，遭患难，成了戏景，叫众人观看；一面陪伴那些受这样苦难的人。
verses.en: At times you were publicly exposed to abuse and afflictions, and at other times you came to share with others who were treated in that way.

verses.zh: 因为你们体恤了那些被捆锁的人，并且你们的家业被人抢去，也甘心忍受，知道自己有更美长存的家业。
verses.en: For in fact you shared the sufferings of those in prison,[NOTE:1] and you accepted the confiscation of your belongings with joy, because you knew that you certainly[NOTE:2] had a better and lasting possession.
notes: Most witnesses, including some significant ones (א D2 1881 M), read δεσμοῖς μου (desmois mou, “my imprisonment”) here, a reading that is probably due to the widespread belief in the early Christian centuries that Paul was the author of Hebrews (cf. Phil 1:7; Col 4:18). It may have been generated by the reading δεσμοῖς without the μου (so P46 Ψ 104), the force of which is so ambiguous (lit., “you shared the sufferings with the bonds”) as to be virtually nonsensical. Most likely, δεσμοῖς resulted when a scribe made an error in copying δεσμίοις (desmiois), a reading which makes excellent sense (“[of] those in prison”) and is strongly supported by early and significant witnesses of the Alexandrian and Western text-forms (A D* H 6 33 81 1739 lat sy co). Thus, δεσμίοις best explains the rise of the other readings on both internal and external grounds and is strongly preferred.
Grk “you yourselves.”

verses.zh: 所以，你们不可丢弃勇敢的心；存这样的心必得大赏赐。
verses.en: So do not throw away your confidence, because it[NOTE:1] has great reward.
notes: Grk “which,” but showing the reason.

verses.zh: 你们必须忍耐，使你们行完了　神的旨意，就可以得着所应许的。
verses.en: For you need endurance in order to do God’s will and so receive what is promised.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “the promise,” referring to the thing God promised, not to the pledge itself.

verses.zh: 因为还有一点点时候，那要来的就来，并不迟延；
verses.en: For just a little longer[NOTE:1] and he who is coming will arrive and not delay.[NOTE:2]
notes: A quotation from Isa 26:20.
A quotation from Hab 2:3.

verses.zh: 只是义人（有古卷：我的义人）必因信得生。他若退后，我心里就不喜欢他。
verses.en: But my righteous one will live by faith, and if he shrinks back, I[NOTE:1] take no pleasure in him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “my soul.”
A quotation from Hab 2:4.

verses.zh: 我们却不是退后入沉沦的那等人，乃是有信心以致灵魂得救的人。
verses.en: But we are not among those who shrink back and thus perish, but are among those who have faith and preserve their souls.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “not…of shrinking back to perdition but of faith to the preservation of the soul.”
